items.titleEn: Managers react to Manchester City’s guilty verdict: ‘Uncertainty is not good for anyone’
items.summaryEn: United manager Carrick rues missing out on ‘emotion in the moment’ while Iraola says he understands why Liverpool fans are angry Continue reading...
bodyEn: Michael Carrick has said retrospectively receiving a winner’s medal would not make up for being robbed of emotional moments of glory by Manchester City’s breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.

Manchester United’s manager was part of the squad that lost out on the Premier League title to City on the final day of the 2011-12 season when Sergio Agüero scored a last-minute winner to secure top spot on goal difference. Carrick and his United teammates were left solemn on the touchline at Sunderland while City, who have been found guilty of breaking financial rules during a nine-year-period between 2009 and 2018, celebrated.

“The emotion, the feeling about winning, a lot of it is in the moment,” Carrick said. “Whether you’re successful, whether you lose, whether it goes against you, that initial [feeling], the beauty of sport and the beauty of football and the beauty of trying to win trophies here, is a little bit on the journey towards it and then the finale, and does it go for you, does it go against you.

“Once that’s done, there’s no getting that back in any direction. The feeling we all crave is coming out on top – that kind of sums it up. Whatever’s done in the past tense is in the past, but in that moment is how you feel in that moment. Certainly as a participant, as a performer, and I’m sure the supporters feel the same, that’s why we love it so much because of the emotion in the moment.”

Carrick was also part of United’s staff under Ole Gunnar Solskjær when they finished second, 22 points behind City, in 2021. City continue to plead their innocence and have appealed against the verdict. If they fail to overturn the independent commission’s ruling, they will probably face a serious punishment.

“It’s affected me personally in different ways,” Carrick said. “But as the case is ongoing now I don’t know where that stands and how it’s going to end up, so we’ll just have to wait and see. What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone’s benefit is essential.” Will Unwin

Andoni Iraola understands the anger among Liverpool supporters towards Manchester City and believes the Premier League needs a resolution to the scandal engulfing English football as swiftly as possible.

Iraola avoided condemning City during his first press conference since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules on an industrial scale over nine years. City have lodged an appeal against the findings and Liverpool’s head coach admitted a final, definitive verdict is essential for the good of the game. “I think it should be [concluded quickly],” he said. “There should be a moment when something comes from this, but now is not that moment. Nobody knows what is going to happen and I think this uncertainty is no good for anyone.”

While refusing to be drawn on the controversy while the legal process is ongoing, Iraola acknowledged the strength of feeling that will be directed at City by Liverpool fans at Anfield on Sunday. City pipped Liverpool to the Premier League title in 2013-14, 2018-19 and 2021-22, the latter two during the fierce rivalry that developed between Jürgen Klopp’s and Pep Guardiola’s teams. Sunday’s reception for the current league leaders promises to be brutal.

“We understand and I understand everything that goes above football,” said Iraola. “Every fan will have their own opinion and attitude towards that but it’s not something that I can control. I need to do my job, to give the best game we can give on the sporting side, so everyone of our supporters is happy on Sunday. I think the challenge of the game for us is big.”

Liverpool’s task on Sunday, as Iraola referenced, will be complicated by the absence of leading goalscorer Alexander Isak and the in-form Cody Gakpo due to injuries sustained on international duty. The two are not long-term absentees but, with Liverpool facing four games in 10 days, they could miss several matches. He admitted: “It’s a bad thing for us, definitely, because both of them have been prolific at the start of the season but the good thing when you coach Liverpool is you still have very good players available. I trust the players we have ready to go. It’s also a good moment for those players to step up, to add good numbers and good performances while we recover Cody and Alex.” Andy Hunter

Vincent Kompany, the former Manchester City captain, insists he is still “really proud” of his success with the club after it was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The Bayern Munich manager won four Premier League titles and multiple domestic cups during his spell at City from 2008 to 2019.
The former Belgium international was a key figure in City’s dominant era under their Abu Dhabi-based owners and is honoured with a statue outside the Etihad Stadium.
“I played 11 years for the club. I’ve loved all of the years I played for the club and everything we achieved and [did] on the pitch – that’s something I’m really proud of,” Kompany said.

Kompany signed for City from Hamburg just weeks before Sheikh Mansour completed a takeover that turned the club from also-rans to serial winners. Asked about the off-pitch issues at his former club, he said: “Everything else, as a player you’re not a part of that and right now as a coach of Bayern Munich I’m not too much occupied with that topic. I’m preparing the game next week and preparing the game we have tomorrow and everything I have as a coach.” Agence France-Presse

Mikel Arteta has insisted his conscience is clear about his time as Manchester City’s assistant manager and promised to “talk with clarity” about his former club when their appeal against a guilty verdict on more than 100 Premier League’s charges has been decided.

Arteta spent more than three years as Pep Guardiola’s assistant at City before moving to Arsenal in December 2019. The Spaniard, who signed a lucrative new four-year contract this week, moved to the Etihad in July 2016 and was part of Guardiola’s backroom staff as they won titles in 2018 and 2019.

The first came during the period in which City breached financial regulations, according to an independent commission. Arteta was reluctant to discuss any potential punishment City could face but was asked whether his conscience was clear from his spell at City and responded: “Yes.”

That was as far as he was prepared to venture after being bombarded with questions about City before Arsenal’s game against Leeds on Saturday. Arteta had been due to deliver a statement at the start of his press conference but the plan changed at the last minute. He refused to be drawn on how he felt when he heard the verdict or whether the uncertainty it had created would have a long-term impact on the Premier League’s brand.

“I want to think that it doesn’t, but I don’t know,” he said. “Uncertainty is not in our control and our control is to bring everything that we can individually through the club to maintain the position that we have to be the best league in the world.”

Arteta added: “The thing is that this has been going for various years. That process is still not finished. So it is very difficult to express how I feel, because it is not resolved. When it is resolved I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel.”

It is understood Arsenal and other Premier League clubs are keen for the situation to be resolved as quickly as possible, although City’s appeal means it could drag on until at least the new year. Arteta also dismissed suggestions Arsenal could be the main beneficiaries should City find themselves relegated, having finished as runners up to them three years in a row before becoming champions last season.
“I think we control our accelerator, and believe me, for seven years it’s been full gas in everything that we can do and take in every corner at maximum speed,” he said. Ed Aarons

Roberto De Zerbi insists he has no time to dwell on Manchester City’s guilty verdict with Tottenham bottom of the table. De Zerbi was a Napoli player when they faced Juventus in the 2006-07 season after Juve were found guilty of match-fixing and relegated to Serie B.

Juventus had an initial 30-point deduction reduced to nine and still won promotion straight back to Serie A. Asked what the experience was like, De Zerbi replied: “I was crazy as a player, I don’t remember my thoughts, just think on the ball, just think on our job.

“When you are a player, you don’t think too much. When you are a coach, the same because the focus is on your players, especially now because we are on the bottom of the table. I have no time to think of the other problems than my team, my club.”

The Spurs manager said the scandal did not change Italian football, and added: “There are the people who have to decide to take the decision, with responsibility, with courage, and honesty, always. It’s not my job. My job is to be a coach. But I love respecting the rules, like all people in our club.”

Dejan Kulusevski is on the verge of returning after more than 500 days out with a complex knee injury. The forward will travel to Manchester for Sunday’s crunch match against United to support the team as he closes in on a comeback.
De Zerbi told his squad in a meeting that Kulusevski had set an example to them. “He’s an inspiration,” he said. “He reacted very well, with character, with courage, with passion.”
De Zerbi said the first week of the three-week international break had been particularly “tough” and that he suffered “a lot”. The 47-year-old took a short holiday but was unable to switch off.
“If you work with passion and work like me, you can’t go home and forget your work, especially in this type of moment – it’s inside you,” he said.
He believes Spurs can replicate Aston Villa, who failed to win any of their first five Premier League games last season before winning 12 of their next 13 and qualifying for the Champions League.
“It’s possible. Why not? But to do what Villa did, we have to click. But I think the first win is not a gift from God. You have to deserve to win. And we didn’t deserve to win so far.” Sam Cunningham

items.titleZh: 各队主帅谈曼城被判违规：不确定性对任何人都没有好处
items.summaryZh: 多位英超主帅谈曼城被判违规，阿尔特塔表示问心无愧，并将等案件彻底结束后再做清晰表达。
bodyZh: 迈克尔·卡里克表示，由于曼城违反了英超财务规则，他错失了当时的情感荣耀时刻，而事后获得冠军奖牌也无法弥补这一点。
这位曼联主帅是2011-12赛季最后一天在积分榜上因净胜球劣势输给曼城的那支球队的成员，当时塞尔吉奥·阿圭罗打入了压哨绝杀。卡里克和他的曼联队友在桑德兰的场边显得十分落寞，而曼城则在庆祝他们被指控在2009年至2018年期间违反财务规则的这九年里所取得的成果。
卡里克说：“那种情感，关于获胜的感觉，很大程度上在于当下。无论你是成功了，还是失败了，或者结果对你不利，最初的感受、体育的美妙、足球的美妙以及在这里努力赢得奖杯的美妙，都在于通往目标的旅程以及最后的结局，看结果是偏向你还是背离你。”
“一旦这一切结束了，就再也无法以任何方式找回那种感觉了。我们所有人渴望的感觉都是登顶——这大致就是全部。过去发生的事情已经成为过去，但在那一刻，你的感觉就是那一刻的感受。当然，作为一名参与者、作为一名表演者，我相信球迷们也有同感，这就是为什么我们如此热爱它，因为它包含了当下的情感。”
在2021年曼联落后曼城22分获得亚军时，卡里克也曾在索尔斯克亚手下的曼联教练组任职。曼城继续坚称自己无辜，并已对裁决提出上诉。如果他们未能推翻独立委员会的裁决，他们可能会面临严重的惩罚。
卡里克说：“这在不同的方面对我的个人产生了影响。但由于案件目前仍在进行中，我不知道它目前的状况如何，最终会如何结束，所以我们只能拭目以待。我要说的是，越早解决这件事对所有人的利益来说都是必不可少的。”
安东尼·伊劳拉理解利物浦球迷对曼城愤怒的心情，并认为英超联赛需要尽快对这桩笼罩着英格兰足球的丑闻做出最终裁决。
在曼城被判定大规模违反英超财务规则后的首场新闻发布会上，伊劳拉避免对曼城进行谴责。曼城已对裁决结果提出上诉，而利物浦主帅承认，一个最终的、决定性的裁决对足球运动的发展至关重要。他说：“我认为应该迅速结案。应该有一个事情尘埃落定的时候，但现在还不是那个时刻。没有人知道会发生什么，我认为这种不确定性对任何人都没有好处。”
虽然在法律程序进行期间拒绝卷入这一争议，但伊劳拉承认，周日利物浦球迷在安菲尔德对曼城时将会流露出强烈的情绪。曼城在2013-14赛季、2018-19赛季和2021-22赛季都曾力压利物浦夺得英超冠军，后两次发生在于克洛普和佩普·瓜迪奥拉的球队之间激烈的竞争时期。周日对现任联赛领头羊的迎接注定将是残酷的。
伊劳拉说：“我们理解，我也理解所有超越足球的事情。每个球迷都会对此有自己的观点和态度，但这并不是我所能控制的。我需要做好我的工作，在竞技层面奉献出我们能给出的最好比赛，这样我们的每一位球迷在周日都会感到高兴。我认为这场比赛对我们来说是一个巨大的挑战。”

正如伊劳拉所提及的，利物浦在周日的任务将因首席射手亚历山大·伊萨克和状态正佳的科迪·加克波因在国际比赛日受伤而缺阵而变得复杂。这两个人并非长期缺阵，但在利物浦10天内要踢4场比赛的情况下，他们可能会错过多场比赛。他承认：“这绝对是一件坏事，因为他们在赛季初都有很高的进球效率，但当你执教利物浦时，好的一面是你仍然有非常优秀的可用球员。我相信我们准备好的球员。在我们恢复科迪和亚历克斯的同时，这也是那些球员挺身而出、贡献出色数据和表现的好时机。”
前曼城队长文森特·孔帕尼坚称，在俱乐部被判定违反英超财务规则后，他依然对自己在俱乐部的成功感到“非常自豪”。这位拜仁慕尼黑主帅在2008年至2019年效力曼城期间赢得了四座英超冠军奖杯以及多项国内杯赛冠军。
这位前比利时国脚是曼城在阿布扎比老板统治下的统治时期的关键人物，并在阿提哈德球场外拥有一座雕像以表彰他的贡献。
孔帕尼说：“我在俱乐部效力了11年。我热爱我在俱乐部效力的所有岁月，以及我们在球场上取得和做到的一切——这是我真正感到自豪的事情。”
在谢赫·曼苏尔完成收购、将曼城从一支碌碌无为的球队转变为常胜将军的几周前，孔帕尼从汉堡转会加盟曼城。当被问及他前俱乐部场外的问题时，他说：“其他所有事情，作为一名球员，你并不是其中的一部分，而现在作为拜仁慕尼黑的主教练，我并没有过多地被这个话题所占据。我正在备战下周的比赛，备战我们明天的比赛，以及作为一名教练我所拥有的一切。”
米克尔·阿尔特塔坚称，对于自己在担任曼城助理教练期间的经历，他问心无愧，并承诺在针对曼城涉及100多项英超指控的有罪裁决的上诉有了结果后，将“清晰地谈论”他的前俱乐部。
在2019年12月转投阿森纳之前，阿尔特塔在瓜迪奥拉手下担任了三年多的曼城助教。这位本周刚签下一份丰厚四年新合同的西班牙人于2016年7月加盟阿提哈德球场，并作为瓜迪奥拉教练组的一员赢得了2018年和2019年的联赛冠军。
根据独立委员会的裁决，第一个冠军正是在曼城违反财务条例的时期获得的。阿尔特塔不愿讨论曼城可能面临的任何潜在惩罚，但当被问及他在曼城期间是否问心无愧时，他回答道：“是的。”
在阿森纳周六对阵利兹联的比赛前，他被关于曼城的各种问题狂轰滥炸，而这也是他愿意表达的极限。阿尔特塔原本计划在新闻发布会开始时发表一份声明，但该计划在最后一刻发生了变化。当被问及听到这一裁决时的感受，或者由此产生的不确定性是否会对英超联赛的品牌产生长期影响时，他拒绝过多发表意见。
他说：“我想认为不会，但我不知道。不确定性不在我们的控制范围内，而我们的控制范围是通过俱乐部个人的全部努力，来保持我们作为世界上最好联赛的地位。”
阿尔特塔补充道：“问题在于这件事已经持续了好几年。这个过程仍未结束。因此，很难表达我的感受，因为它尚未解决。当它解决时，我可以清晰地谈论并确切地告诉你我的感受。”
据了解，阿森纳和其他英超联赛俱乐部都希望这一局面能够尽快得到解决，尽管曼城的上诉意味着这可能会拖延到至少新年。阿尔特塔还驳斥了关于如果曼城遭到降级、阿森纳将成为主要受益者的说法，此前阿森纳连续三个赛季屈居亚军，并在上赛季夺得冠军。
他说：“我认为我们控制着自己的油门，相信我，七年来我们在所有能够做到和抓住的方面都以最大速度全速前进。”
罗伯托·德泽尔比坚称，由于热刺目前处于积分榜垫底，他没有时间去纠结曼城的有罪裁决。在2006-07赛季尤文图斯因假球案被判有罪并降入意乙时，德泽尔比曾效力于那不勒斯并与尤文交手。
尤文图斯最初被扣除30分后减至9分，但仍然直接升回意甲。当被问及那段经历是怎样的时，德泽尔比回答：“我当球员时很疯狂，我不记得我的想法了，只想着足球，只想着我们的工作。”
“当你是一名球员时，你不会想太多。当你是一名教练时也是如此，因为焦点都在你的球员身上，尤其是现在因为我们排在积分榜垫底。除了我的球队、我的俱乐部，我没有时间去思考其他问题。”
热刺主帅表示，这起丑闻并没有改变意大利足球，并补充道：“总有人必须做出决定，带着责任感、勇气和诚实，永远如此。这不是我的工作。我的工作是做一名教练。但我热爱遵守规则，就像我们俱乐部所有人一样。”
德扬·库卢塞夫斯基在因膝伤缺阵500多天后即将复出。这位前锋将前往曼彻斯特观看周日对阵曼联的焦点战，以在即将复出之际支持球队。
德泽尔比在一次会议上告诉他的全队，库卢塞夫斯基为他们树立了榜样。他说：“他是一个激励。他反应得很好，充满个性、勇气和激情。”
德泽尔比表示，为期三周的国际比赛日的第一周格外“艰难”，他“承受了很大痛苦”。这位47岁的主帅进行了短暂的度假，但无法让自己彻底放松。
他说：“如果你带着激情工作，像我一样工作，你回家后就无法忘记工作，特别是在这种类型的时刻——它已经融入了你的内心。”
他相信热刺可以复制阿斯顿维拉的轨迹，维拉在上赛季前五场英超联赛一场未胜的情况下，随后的13场比赛赢下了12场并获得了欧冠资格。
“这是可能的。为什么不呢？但要做到维拉所做的事情，我们必须产生化学反应。但我认为第一场胜利不是上帝的恩赐。你必须配得上胜利。而到目前为止，我们还配不上胜利。”

items.titleEn: Preview: Arsenal v Leeds United
items.summaryEn: Get the team news, stats, live coverage, tactics and more before we face the Whites in the Premier League at Emirates Stadium
bodyEn: After a three-week wait, the Premier League is finally back as we host Leeds United on Saturday (12.30pm).

The extended break means it'll be 34 days since our supporters last filtered through the Emirates Stadium turnstiles, and after being starved of chances to support us, news of Mikel Arteta’s new contract will only heighten the hunger to roar us back to winning ways.

The form book would suggest we have a good chance of doing that, as we have won each of the last seven league meetings with the Whites by an aggregate score of 24-5. However, Daniel Farke’s team have yet to lose this term and will come to N5 to seek a win on our patch for the first time in 23 years.
WHITES’ CLEAN RECORD

After five games, Leeds are unbeaten in fifth place, and could start a top-flight campaign without losing in their first six for the first time since 2001. Their good form stretches back further, as they have lost only one of their last 14 league games, pulling away from the drop zone in the final months of their first season back at this level to finish 14th.

Farke strengthened his defence through the arrivals of James Trafford in goal plus centre-backs Tarik Muharemovic and Nico Elvedi, and an 88th-minute free-kick from Anton Stach beat Nottingham Forest on the opening day to hand them the perfect start, before 1-1 draws with fellow high-flyers Brentford and Brighton.

They then dismantled Newcastle United 4-1 at Elland Road before going into the international break with a goalless home draw with Crystal Palace. After beating Forest again in the second round of the Carabao Cup, they were knocked out 6-3 by Chelsea, despite leading twice in a crazy tie.
WHAT THE MANAGERS SAY

Arteta: "The pain [from Brighton] is still there in the tummy, and tomorrow we certainly have to play with that. It was a lesson for us when you don't hit certain basics, especially against a really good side. You become almost unrecognisable, and it can happen. But it's been more about learning from who we are and how thin the line is, from being exceptional to becoming very average.

"I think [Leeds] fully deserve where they are because they've earned it. They are there because I think they merit it with a lot of great things that they've done throughout matches to be better than the opponent. We know their qualities, we talked to [the players] in the last two days, and we are fully ready for it."

Farke: "I think again we are not the favourite in this game, no question, but to be very honest, Arsenal last season was more or less the only team where we had no chance to win one of the games; we were not even close to it. It's a good chance to see if we have edged a bit closer and are also competitive in such a game.

"The whole stadium will buzz [after the] announcement of Mikel's contract. It's the worst possible moment to play such a game but you can't pick and you take it. It's a good chance for us to show how far we have come over the last year now, and we travel respectful, but not with fear.”
TEAM NEWS

Christos Tzolis is out of the game after he was forced to withdraw with an injury during Greece's draw with the Netherlands during the break, with Arteta revealing he is set to miss a few weeks. Meanwhile, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa also returned from Germany and England duty prematurely and they continue to be assessed.

Declan Rice sat out Three Lions duty to recover from some niggles and could also be available, while Ben White is back in training after recovering from the groin injury that forced him to miss the Brighton game. William Saliba remains out with his back issue.
As for Leeds, Welsh duo Daniel James (back) and Joe Rodon (hamstring) are both out, but Harry Wilson is back in contention after missing the international break with a quadricep injury.
Winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya picked up an ankle issue on duty with France’s under-21s but Farke believes it’s not too bad and should be available.
TALKING TACTICS

Adrian Clarke, writing in the official matchday programme: Farke’s switch to 3-5-2 last November was a tactical masterstroke, losing just five of their 32 league matches since. The shape is designed primarily to nullify opponents, with at least eight starters known for their defensive resilience.

Leeds are a robust, physically dominant outfit. Using a solid 5-3-2 off the ball, they turn the ball over regularly, thanks to a tigerish midfield trio constantly pressuring their opposite numbers, especially Ethan Ampadu and Stach. Statistically, Leeds rank second in press sequences so far this term, so we can expect them to close us down with hostility.

Discipline and concentration mean they’re the only Premier League side yet to make an error leading to a shot. That, plus having so many players comfortable in their off-the-ball work, limits the quality of chances they face, and their average of 0.09xG per shot faced is the second-best tally behind us.

However, starting with two or three natural attacking players means creating goalscoring opportunities hasn't been easy, and only three sides have managed fewer shots on target than their 18. Despite this, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor have struck up a terrific rapport as the front two, and the former is excellent at sniffing out where to be inside the box, has searing pace and is top class in the air.
FACTS AND STATS
We have won nine of our last 10 Premier League games against Leeds United, including each of the last seven by an aggregate score of 24-5.

Leeds have lost each of their last five away games against us since a 3-2 victory in May 2003, conceding at least four goals in four of those. That has happened nine times in Premier League meetings between us, with only us against Everton (12) and Manchester United v Newcastle (11) seeing more.
We have won eight of our last nine league home games, keeping a clean sheet in six of those victories.
Leeds are winless in 14 Premier League matches in London (D4 L10), since a 2-1 victory against Brentford in May 2022.

Mikel Arteta has won all four of his games against Daniel Farke, his joint-best 100%-win rate against a manager in the top-flight (level with Gary O’Neil), and Farke’s worst 100%-loss rate against a manager during his league career in England.

Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz have both scored in each of our two home league games this season; only one previous occasion has any side seen two teammates score in their opening three home matches of a Premier League campaign: Newcastle’s Andy Cole and Rob Lee in 1994/95.
Odegaard has assisted four goals in his last six games against Leeds United, and has assisted more often against Chelsea and West Ham (both 5).
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has scored seven goals in his last 11 league games, though only one has been away from home.
MATCH OFFICIALS

Paul Tierney will be the man in the middle for this one, and we are currently on an eight-game unbeaten run with him in charge, stretching back to April 9. He last visited Emirates Stadium for our title-clinching 1-0 win against Burnley in May, and the only other time he refereed us last term was the 2-2 draw at Wolves in February.

The Lancashire-based official is less familiar to Leeds, having been handed three Whites games in three years. Two came last season, and they won both - beating Birmingham City on penalties in the FA Cup and Manchester United at Old Trafford in April.
Referee: Paul TierneyAssistants: Richard West, Steve MeredithFourth official: Oliver LangfordVAR: Tony HarringtonAssistant VAR: Nick Greenhalgh
PREVIOUS VISITS FROM LEEDS

You have to go back to May 2003 for the last time Leeds returned north with three points from N5, and they have never won on four top-flight visits to Emirates Stadium - only Stoke City (10) and Bolton Wanderers (6) are on a longer run.

Leeds have also not kept a clean sheet in any of their last 15 in N5, a run that continued last season when we kicked off our home campaign with a 5-0 win against Farke’s team, with Jurrien Timber and Viktor Gyokeres netting braces, while Bukayo Saka added the other.

In April 2023, two goals from Gabriel Jesus as well as strikes from Ben White and Granit Xhaka saw us run out 4-1 victors, while the season before it was Eddie Nketiah who helped himself to a pair of goals, paving the way for a 2-1 success towards the end of 2021/22.

items.titleZh: 赛事前瞻：阿森纳主场迎战利兹联
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳将在英超主场迎战利兹联，阿尔特塔的新合同及伤病情况备受关注。
bodyZh: 经过三周的等待，英超联赛终于回归，我们将于周六（下午12点30分）主场迎战利兹联。
这段延长的间歇期意味着距离我们球迷上次踏入酋长球场已经过去了34天，在经历了一段时间的观赛空窗期后，米克尔·阿尔特塔续约的消息无疑将进一步点燃大家重回胜利轨道的渴望。
交锋记录表明我们很有希望做到这一点，因为我们最近七次在联赛中对阵利兹联保持全胜，总比分为24-5。不过，丹尼尔·法尔克率领的球队本赛季至今保持不败，他们将来到N5区，力争23年来首次在我们的主场带走胜利。
利兹联的清白记录
经过五场比赛后，利兹联保持不败并排名第五，他们有望自2001年以来首次在顶级联赛开局前六场保持不败。他们的良好状态延续得更久，在过去的14场联赛中只输了一场，在上赛季重返英超的最后几个月里成功远离降级区并最终排名第14位。
法尔克通过引进门将詹姆斯·特拉福德以及中后卫塔里克·穆哈雷莫维奇和尼科·埃尔维迪加强了防守，安东·斯塔赫在首轮比赛第88分钟的任意球破门帮助他们击败诺丁汉森林，取得了完美开局，随后他们又以1-1分别战平了同为表现出色的布伦特福德和布赖顿。
接着他们在埃兰路球场4-1大胜纽卡斯尔联，随后在国际比赛日前与水晶宫互交白卷。在联赛杯第二轮再次击败森林后，他们在与切尔西的疯狂对决中虽然两度领先，但最终以3-6被淘汰。
主教练言论
阿尔特塔：“这种痛楚（来自布赖顿的失利）依然留在肚子里，明天我们肯定带着这种情绪去比赛。这对我们是一个教训，当你在某些基本环节上没有做到位时，特别是面对一支真正出色的球队，你会变得几乎面目全非，这种情况确实会发生。但这更多的是关于吸取教训，认清自我，以及从卓越沦为平庸之间的差距是多么微小。”
“我认为（利兹联）完全配得上他们现在的位置，因为这是他们应得的。他们能站在那里是因为他们在比赛中做出了很多伟大的事情，表现得比对手更好。我们了解他们的实力，我们在过去两天里与（球员们）进行了交流，我们已经做好了充分的准备。”
法尔克：“我认为毫无疑问我们在这场比赛中不是热门，但老实说，上赛季的阿森纳可以说是唯一一支让我们毫无取胜机会的球队；我们甚至连接近都谈不上。这是一个很好的机会，可以检验我们是否稍微缩小了差距，并且在这样的比赛中具备竞争力。”
“在宣布米克尔续约后，整个球场都会沸腾。踢这样一场比赛的时机再糟糕不过了，但你没得挑，只能接受。这对我们来说是一个好机会，可以展示我们在过去一年里取得了多大的进步，我们带着敬意前往，但绝不畏惧。”
球队新闻
克里斯托斯·齐奥利斯在代表希腊队与荷兰队的比赛中因伤退场，将缺席本场比赛，阿尔特塔透露他预计将缺阵数周。与此同时，凯·哈弗茨和埃兹里·孔萨也提前结束了德国队和英格兰队的任务归队，目前仍在接受评估。
德克兰·赖斯缺席了三狮军团的比赛以从一些小伤中恢复，本场比赛可能复出。本·怀特在从腹股沟伤势中恢复后已经恢复训练，此前该伤势迫使他缺席了对阵布赖顿的比赛。威廉·萨利巴由于背部问题依然缺阵。
至于利兹联，威尔士双星丹尼尔·詹姆斯（背部）和乔·罗登（腿筋）均告缺阵，但哈里·威尔逊在因四头肌受伤错过国际比赛日后重新回到大名单候选行列中。
边锋让-马特奥·巴霍亚在法国U21国家队效力时遭遇脚踝问题，但法尔克认为伤势不重，应该可以出场。
战术探讨
阿德里安·克拉克在官方比赛日场刊中写道：法尔克去年11月改打3-5-2阵型是一次战术上的神来之笔，在此后的32场联赛中他们仅输了五场。这一阵型主要旨在压制对手，首发阵容中至少有八名以防守顽强著称的球员。
利兹联是一支身体强壮、对抗占优的球队。在无球状态下采用稳固的5-3-2阵型，凭借由埃丹·阿帕杜和斯塔赫等球员组成、不断向对手施压的凶悍中场三人组，他们能够频繁完成抢断。从数据上看，利兹联本赛季至今的高位逼抢序列排名第二，因此我们可以预见他们将对我们展开凶猛的围抢。
纪律性和专注度意味着他们是本赛季唯一一支尚未出现导致对手射门失误的英超球队。这一点，再加上众多擅长无球跑动的球员，限制了他们所面对的射门质量，他们场均面对对手射门的预期进球数为0.09，仅次于我们，排名第二位。
然而，由于首发阵容中只有两到三名纯正的攻击手，创造进球机会并非易事，只有三支球队的射门次数比他们的18次还要少。尽管如此，多米尼克·卡尔弗特-卢因和诺亚·奥卡福作为锋线双箭头已经培养出了极佳的默契，前者在禁区内寻找落点能力极强，速度极快且头球顶尖。
数据与事实
我们在最近10场对阵利兹联的英超比赛中赢了9场，其中包括最近的7连胜，总比分为24-5。
自从2003年5月客场3-2取胜以来，利兹联在我们这里遭遇了客场五连败，其中有四场比赛至少丢了四球。在我们两队的英超交锋中，这种情况已经发生了九次，仅次于我们对阵埃弗顿（12次）以及曼联对阵纽卡斯尔（11次）。
我们在最近9个联赛主场中赢了8场，其中6场保持零封。
自2002年5月客场2-1击败布伦特福德以来，利兹联在伦敦的14场英超比赛中一场未胜（4平10负）。
米克尔·阿尔特塔对阵丹尼尔·法尔克的4场比赛全部获胜，这是他在顶级联赛中对阵单一主帅并保持100%胜率的最高纪录（与加里·奥尼尔并列），这也是法尔克在英格兰联赛执教生涯中对阵单一主帅的100%全败最差纪录。
马丁·厄德高和凯·哈弗茨本赛季在我们前两个主场联赛中均有进球；此前在英超联赛历史上，只有一支球队的两位队友在主场前三场比赛中都有过进球：1994/95赛季纽卡斯尔的安迪·科尔和罗布·李。
厄德高在最近6场对阵利兹联的比赛中送出了4次助攻，他在对阵切尔西和西汉姆联时助攻次数更多（均为5次）。
多米尼克·卡尔弗特-卢因在最近11场联赛中打入7球，但其中只有1球是在客场打进的。
比赛裁判
保罗·蒂尔尼将担任本场比赛的主裁判，在我们由他执法的情况下，目前正处于一场八场不败的纪录中，该纪录可追溯到4月9日。他上一次造访酋长球场是在5月我们1-0击败伯恩利锁定联赛冠军的比赛中，而上赛季他执法我们的另一场比赛是2月客场2-2战平狼队。
这位来自兰开夏郡的裁判对利兹联相对陌生，过去三年只执法过三场利兹联的比赛。其中两场在上赛季，他们都取得了胜利——在足总杯中点球击败伯明翰城，以及4月在老特拉福德球场击败曼联。
主裁判：保罗·蒂尔尼；助理裁判：理查德·韦斯特、史蒂夫·梅雷迪思；第四官员：奥利弗·兰福德；视频助理裁判（VAR）：托尼·哈灵顿；助理视频助理裁判：尼克·格林哈尔格
利兹联过往造访记录
你需要追溯到2003年5月，才能看到利兹联从N5区带走三分的最后一次场景，而且他们从未在酋长球场的四次顶级联赛访问中取胜——只有斯托克城（10次）和博尔顿（6次）的连续不胜纪录更长。
利兹联在N5区的最近15场比赛中也从未保持过零封，这一纪录在上赛季延续了下来，当时我们在主场揭幕战中5-0大胜法尔克的球队，尤里恩·廷贝尔和维克托·哲凯赖什梅开二度，布卡约·萨卡攻入另一球。
2003年4月，加布里埃尔·热苏斯的两粒进球以及本·怀特和格兰特·扎卡的破门帮助我们4-1大胜对手，而在前一个赛季，正是埃迪·恩凯蒂亚独中两元，为2021/22赛季末2-1的胜利铺平了道路。
现场直播
随着英超联赛重回酋长球场，《来自N5的直播》（Live From N5）节目回归Arsenal.com和阿森纳官方App！
请在开赛前一小时加入妮可·霍利迪和热雷米·阿利亚迭雷的直播，演员阿萨·巴特费尔德、喜剧演员莫·吉利根以及厨师兼社交媒体明星萨姆·霍兰德将为演播室增添更多星光。
我们将重温大卫·拉亚加入妮可和弗里米在Sobha沙发上的场景，米克尔·阿尔特塔将被尊为我们的“本周英雄”，现场观众还将在时间胶囊和阿森纳大脑环节接受考验。
随后，当比赛正式打响时，丹·罗伯克和阿德里安·克拉克将提供现场解说和专业分析——请确保调好频道。

items.titleEn: Arteta on his absolute passion and love for the game
items.summaryEn: Mikel Arteta has said that he continues to love the beautiful game just as much as ever.
bodyEn: After signing a contract extension as our manager on Wednesday, Mikel Arteta has said that he continues to love the beautiful game just as much as ever.
The boss didn’t have to think twice about putting pen to paper on a new deal due to his absolute passion for making us better.

That’s the message he was getting across in his pre-Leeds United press conference at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Friday, in which he was asked about the biggest lesson he has learned about himself over the past seven years.

“That probably you put a lot of focus on the things that you need to do, you need to help to do, to transform the football club to the vision of the idea that you have,” he replied. “And the reality is that within that period there is a huge personal transformation as well that is needed in order to get where you want to get.

“It's probably been one of the most fascinating things, because you don't do that by yourself, you do it with the people that are next to you, and I'm very, very lucky to have the people that are next to me.”

Asked if he could go back in time and deliver a message to the 2019 version of Mikel, who had just became Arsenal manager for the first time, he added: “Go for it! Don't even doubt. But I think it's natural, that fear when it's something unknown for you. It’s the first time you're going to do it, it's huge, it can be so much responsibility, but you never know.
“But if you feel it's the right thing to do, and the purpose and the reason why you do it is right, I think it's worth taking the risk and going for it.”
As the Premier League’s longest-serving manager, Mikel was also asked whether he thinks he will need to take a break at some point, or whether he could go on for the next 10-15 years.

“A break? To stop doing what I do? At the moment, it’s not in my head, because I love so much what I do,” he said. “I wake up every morning and I have this energy. A lot of people say, ‘Mikel, you need to rest sometimes on this.’ But the reality, and I'm honest, sometimes I take a break during the day, I go back and I start to work on something, I get more energy because I love what I do.
“What about this? What about if we pass on that? This is the beauty of not working, of doing something that is your absolute passion, and that's why I feel extremely lucky to be where I am.

“I think I'm still really young, and this is just my first experience as well, and that is probably the way I live my profession. This week we had a lot of discussion, and people talked about pressure or stress, and I understand. I don't relate my job to that. I've been through very different moments, but it's more about the level of the passion and love that I have for the game and what I do, with the ambition and drive and aspirations that I have, and if you want to put a name into it, fine.
“But for me, it's just a privilege to do that every single day. If one day it’s not, then it will be as well my decision to say ‘okay, now I’m not enjoying it, it’s time to stop.’”

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔谈他对足球运动的无限激情与热爱
items.summaryZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔表示，他对足球这项美丽运动的热爱一如既往。
bodyZh: 在周三签下了一份担任我们主教练的续约合同后，米克尔·阿尔特塔表示，他对这项美丽运动的热爱一如既往。
由于对让我们变得更好的绝对激情，这位主帅在签署新合同前没有丝毫犹豫。
这是他在周五于索布哈地产业训练基地举行的对阵利兹联赛前新闻发布会上传达的信息，会上他被问及在过去七年里关于自我最大的收获是什么。
他回答说：“那可能意味着你把很多精力放在你需要做的事情上，你需要提供帮助去完成的事情上，从而将这家足球俱乐部转变为你心中的愿景和理念。现实情况是，在这个过程中，为了达到你想要的高度，也需要经历巨大的个人转变。”
“这可能是最迷人的事情之一，因为你不是独自完成这些的，你是与你身边的伙伴共同完成的，而我非常、非常幸运能拥有身边的这些伙伴。”
当被问及如果能够回到过去，向2019年刚刚首次成为阿森纳主教练的那个米克尔传达一句话时，他补充道：“去吧！甚至不要怀疑。但我认为这是很自然的，当面对未知事物时会感到恐惧。这是你第一次做这件事，任务极其重大，责任可能非常巨大，但你永远不会知道结果。”
“但如果你觉得这是正确的事情，并且你这样做的目的和原因也是正确的，我认为冒这个险去尝试是值得的。”
作为英超执教时间最长的现任主教练，米克尔还被问及他是否认为自己在某个阶段需要休息，或者他是否能继续执教未来10到15年。
他说道：“休息？停止做我正在做的事？目前这并没有在我的脑海中出现，因为我太热爱我所做的事情了。我每天早晨醒来都充满能量。很多人说，‘米克尔，有时候你需要在这些事情上休息一下。’但现实是，说实话，有时我在白天休息一下，然后回去开始做一些事情时，我会获得更多的能量，因为我热爱我所做的事情。”
“这个怎么样？如果我们把那个传过去会怎样？这就是不工作的魅力所在，做一件你倾注绝对激情的事，这就是为什么我觉得自己身处目前这个位置极其幸运。”
“我认为我还非常年轻，这也是我的第一次执教经历，这可能就是我对待职业生涯的方式。这周我们进行了很多讨论，人们谈论压力或紧张，我能理解。我并没有把我的工作和那些联系在一起。我经历过非常不同的时刻，但这更多是关于我对比赛和我所做事情的激情与热爱程度，以及我所拥有的雄心、动力和抱负，如果你想给它起个名字，那也行。”
“但对我来说，每天能做这件事本身就是一种特权。如果有一天不再如此，那么这将同样是我的决定，我会说‘好吧，我现在不享受了，是时候停下来了。’ ”

items.titleEn: Every word of Arteta's pre-Leeds press conference
items.summaryEn: Mikel Arteta was back in front of the media at the Sobha Realty Training Centre for his pre-Leeds United press conference
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta was back in front of the media at the Sobha Realty Training Centre for his pre-Leeds United press conference on Friday.
The boss faced questions about Manchester City's charges, his contract extension as our manager, the visit of Leeds and more.
Here's everything he had to say on the following subjects...

on the Man City charges:I fully understand the question, but obviously I think it's very important that we respect the process and the timelines. It's still an ongoing process that is not resolved, because it's been appealed, and my position, and the club's position, is not to make any further comments until this is fully resolved.

on how the noise will affect Manchester City:I don't know, that's something that's not in our hands. In our hands is the way we have prepared since all the internationals are back, to be in the best possible condition to be better than Leeds tomorrow and beat them. That's where the focus has been.

on his new contract:Extremely honoured. My family and I are very grateful to continue to enjoy this unbelievable ride that I started almost seven years ago. I loved not the outcome, because when there are two parties and you have to resolve a situation, I said from the beginning that both the club and I wanted the same thing, but I loved the manner that it was handled. I think it's really important.

I always say that when you are negotiating and trying to figure out the future, the most important thing is at the end. When you are about to sign the deal, you look at everyone in the room and see some smiley faces and excitement in their eyes. That's what I gather from Stan and Josh, especially, and then from Rich, from James, from Andrea, and then obviously the staff and the players. And that's it. I have to earn the right every single day to continue to be at this level, sitting in this chair and making the most out of it.

on building a dynasty:It's something that you have to earn daily. We know what the level is right now; we know where the standards lie; we know what the expectations are. But the good thing is the level of enthusiasm, passion and energy is even higher. That's what we want to accomplish all together, and that's the opportunity ahead of us.

on whether bringing the club together is his proudest achievement:Yes, in the manner that we've done it all together, and everybody feeling part of something that is very, very connected right now. Then that the club has a very clear identity and ambition and a pathway where we want to go. I think that's very, very important as well.

on whether he can do 20 more years:It's today and hopefully tomorrow, and this is how we have to live this job. I think what you have to do is enjoy the journey - I think it's the most important thing and probably the biggest lesson that I had over the last seven years. The biggest gift that I had throughout this period has been the people around me to make me feel loved and allow me to enjoy what I do.

on Declan Rice’s fitness:We have to manage him because he's had a few issues since he's come back from the World Cup, and we know the amount of games he's played in the last three years. It was the sensible thing to do, and hopefully tomorrow he's available but some others are in doubt.

on Havertz, Konsa and Tzolis injuries:With Kai, he had a muscular injury, so I spoke to Jurgen [Klopp] and immediately they sent the player back, as is normal. Ezri has been carrying some issues as well and we had good communication with the England camp about that. Tzolis has a muscle injury, and he's going to be out for a few weeks. He's not available yet.

on Hincapie and Mosquera fitness:They are both available. They did incredibly well to be available for the Brighton game, but we decided not to use them at the end, especially in the manner that we had to play the last few minutes, but they are both available. And Ben White is available as well.

on the biggest lesson he has learnt about himself over past seven years:That probably you put a lot of focus on the things that you need to do, you need to help to do, to transform the football club, to the vision of the idea that you have. And the reality that within that period there is a huge personal transformation as well that is needed in order to get where you want to get. It's probably been one of the most fascinating things, because you don't do that by yourself, you do it with the people that are next to you, and I'm very, very lucky to have the people that are next to me.

on what he would say to the Mikel of 2019:Go for it! Don't even doubt. But I think it's natural, that fear when it's something unknown for you. It’s the first time you're going to do it, it's huge, it can be so much responsibility, but you never know. But if you feel it's the right thing to do, and the purpose and the reason why you do it is right, I think it's worth taking the risk and going for it.

on the defeat to Brighton:The pain is still there in the tummy, and tomorrow we certainly have to play with that. It was a lesson for us, it was a lot to learn from that game, when you don't hit certain basics in a football match, especially against a really good side. You become almost unrecognisable, and it can happen. But it's been more about learning from who we are and how thin the line is, from being exceptional to becoming very average, and that's a reality. But as well, just realising that with the difficult context that we have, with all the internationals that we've had, what we've done in the first eight weeks, I think it's been remarkable. But, a big attention, because things change very quickly.

on if he is surprised by Leeds’ start to the season:When I watch their games, no. I think they fully deserve where they are because they've earned it, and they are there because I think they merit with a lot of great things that they've done throughout matches to be better than the opponent. We know their qualities, we talked to [the players] in the last two days, and we are fully ready for it.

on his thoughts of a 12.30pm kick off:12.30 is great. We've been three weeks with no football for us! I don't know, the internationals, I don't care without club football, we play at the Emirates in front of our people. So the way and the atmosphere that we have created in recent months has been unbelievable, and we need to make sure that we start by creating that. I'm sure our supporters will be very excited to watch the team play.

on his message to the supporters:My message is very clear, that we have pain in the tummy for what happened in Brighton and it's on us as well to get the pain that they still feel out of it. It's our responsibility and we need to give to them now.

on how he settled into the job at Arsenal:Going through different stages and different moments. I think I've been driven by the passion and the love that I have for this club and because I had a dream which was to become a coach, a manager. This club gave me the opportunity to be at the highest level straight away and I was ready to do anything just to make it work. I think I got the right people around me to cover all the deficiencies or the things that I don't know, to help me to be better and to help the players and the club in every possible way to improve every single day and to instil that culture, that identity and that ambition.

on keeping Max Dowman grounded:I think that's a collective responsibility. First of all, for the parents, because they are the ones that spend the most time with them, and they are already giving the education to be how he is today, and then everybody that works around him. But I don't think that Max has a lot of signs to be worried about because what he wants to do is play football as well as he possibly can at the highest level, and his focus is there.

on whether he feels his time at Manchester City is tainted:I understand the question where they're coming from. There's a lot of noise around it. It's an ongoing process that is not resolved yet and I think we need to respect it and certainly I have to respect that.

on whether he has had to address it with his players:It is not in our hands. The only thing that we can do is focus on everything that we can do to be the best as we possibly can and to be better than any other opponent and that's where we put the energy.

on how important it is to be resolved this season:People are responsible to manage this process and to come to the right conclusions. I'm sure it will be done and it will be resolved in the right way. We have to trust that.

on what was spoken about during his contract negotiations:I'm talking about how we feel about each other. The way we have analysed what we've done together and especially how we're going to take this club to be the best in the world for many years and the platforms, the good things that we have and then you just have a sense how you feel about each other, how we do things. I feel really lucky having Stan and George in front of you, and talking to them and expressing what they want to do, how they want to do it, especially, it's just inspiring. And then there are things that relating to me but the coaching staff as well and how they value the people around it and what is being done from both sides. It's just total alignment. That's why when I see somebody happy after a few months of having discussions and ideas and is it the best thing to do and for how long and other things that have to be discussed. I was just moved because everybody looked happy. I was immensely happy, my family as well, which is the most important thing, but the staff, the people around, the players and them as well. I think that's very important, not only the outcome.

on why he is confident enough to aim for dominance:That's what we want to try to achieve. That's the ambition, and I don't think you have to hide it. The thing is that you have to aim for it every single day and this football, but your aspirations and your dreams are where they are. I think it's easier to get them because if I told you the ones that I had when I arrived, probably you would say: "what are you talking about?" But that was ambition, that's the drive and it's because we believe that we can do it. Then there will be many factors that would allow us or not to achieve it. Time will tell, but certainly that drive is there.

on whether he is relieved to have won the title on the pitch last season:I feel very proud and I feel very emotional when I think especially how we’ve done it and the moments that we have to go through actually to achieve it. It’s a unique and a genuine feeling that I have because of the manner that we did it.

on whether he had any doubts about signing a new contract:You have to sometimes stop and think about how long can you do this, and not only doing it here, but it’s for yourself. Do you have the right level of desire, the energy, the people around you, the way they look at you when you talk? My feeling was yes, and if that feeling changes one day, we’ll look in our eyes, and that’s it. It’s simple.

on whether he thinks the Premier League is damaged:There is a process there again that is not resolved. It's ongoing and we can have a much clearer opinion once it's been resolved. Up to now, I'm not prepared to make any comments

on whether he thinks he will want a break at some point:A break? To stop doing what I do? At the moment, it’s not in my head, because I love so much what I do. I wake up every morning and I have this energy. A lot of people say: "Mikel, you need to rest sometimes." But the reality, and I'm honest, sometimes I take a break during the day, I go back and I start to work on something, I get more energy because I love what I do. What about this? What about if we pass on that? This is the beauty of not working, of doing something that is your absolute passion, and that's why I feel extremely lucky to be where I am.

on whether he could go on for 10, 15 years in the job:I don't know. I think I'm still really young, and this is just my first experience as well, and that is probably the way I live my profession. This week we had a lot of discussion, and people talked about pressure or stress, and I understand. I don't relate my job to that. I've been through very different moments, but it's more about the level of the passion and love that I have for the game and what I do, with the ambition and drive and aspirations that I have, and if you want to put a name to it, fine. But for me, it's just a privilege to do that every single day. If one day it’s not, then it will be also my decision to say: "OK, now I’m not enjoying it, it’s time to stop."
on whether he thinks this is the best league in the world:100%.

on how important the strict financial rules are in the Premier League:I just responded to it, it is the best league in the world, in my opinion, for many reasons, and because I've been here for over 20 years. It will continue to be the best league in the world. Again, I feel privileged to be where I am, and the fact that there are other clubs that have been extremely good at managing their resources in such intelligent and efficient ways. That is good because it has increased the competition, and we saw that a few weeks ago.

on what he learned from the Brighton game:Two things. First of all, the first one about the game, I already mentioned it, and then how good our players are, because when I watched them travelling the world, playing with different national teams, and the incredible impact that they had for the national teams, it gives you reassurance as well. Then, when they come, they have big smiles on their faces, so they feel at home, and they are happy to come, and this is a great thing to feel.
on the fitness of Dowman, Havertz and Konsa:Max is available, Ezri and Kai we will see tomorrow.

on whether the noise surrounding Man City could help us:What we think is about us, about what we do, and what we want to achieve. That's it. The rest is something that we don't control, we have never controlled it, and we don't want to control it. That's the beauty of what we do, but at the end a lot of things depend on us, and that's where we want to leave it.
on whether he has spoken to Pep:We’re going to talk about that, using a different thing that is happening. I prefer not to answer those questions.

on how he views his own evolution over seven years:With the transformation of a football club or a squad of people that we had around the club, obviously comes a personal transformation at every level. Doing something that you've never done in your life, moving your family, starting to build and create something that you very passionately believe that it will make a lot of people happy.

Then experiencing some difficult times along the way, getting up again and dragging people with you with the same purpose, and having some incredible moments together. That shapes you, it’s inevitable. It's been one of the best things, it's been a gift through that journey. I want to experience many more transformations and evolutions because this is why we are here, to continue to learn, to be curious and to help people enjoy this incredible game.

on how inspiring players and staff:I always loved it. When it's against difficulty and when you have to bring people with you, I think that's the nicest thing in our job. To bring people on the journey, to make them feel part of something, to have a very clear purpose and then going through stages where, chapter by chapter, you start to get closer to achieving them all, go again and reinvent yourself and do that. Then there is the way the game has evolved and how you evolve with the game and can you be ahead of the game. That's a constant challenge as well, especially with the level of managers and teams that we have in the league, and that's not going to stop. So that's not going to allow you to stop as well.

items.titleZh: 阿尔特塔赛前新闻发布会全记录
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳主帅阿尔特塔在索布哈 realty 训练基地出席了对阵利兹联的赛前新闻发布会，谈到了球队伤病、新合同以及曼城指控等话题。
bodyZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔周五重返索布哈 realty 训练基地，出席了对阵利兹联队的赛前新闻发布会。
这位主帅面临了关于曼城指控、他作为我们主帅的续约合同、利兹联的来访等问题的质询。
以下是他对以下主题的所有发言……
关于曼城的指控：我完全理解这个问题，但显然我认为非常重要的一点是，我们要尊重程序和时间表。这仍然是一个尚未解决的进行中的程序，因为它已经受到了上诉，而我的立场以及俱乐部的立场是，在事情完全解决之前不作任何进一步的评论。
关于这些杂音将如何影响曼城：我不知道，这不是我们能掌控的。在我们掌控之中的是我们自从所有国脚归队以来的备战方式，以便以最佳状态在明天表现得比利兹联更好并击败他们。这就是我们的焦点所在。
关于他的新合同：感到非常荣幸。我和我的家人非常感谢能够继续享受我近七年前开始这段令人难以置信的旅程。我不喜欢那个结果，因为当有两方并且你必须解决一个情况时，我从一开始就说过俱乐部和我都想要同样的东西，但我喜欢处理这件事的方式。我认为这非常重要。
我总是说，当你处于谈判并试图弄清楚未来时，最重要的是最后。当你即将签署合协议时，你看房间里的每个人，看到一些笑脸和他们眼中的兴奋。这就是我从斯坦和乔什身上感受到的，尤其是里奇、詹姆斯、安德烈，然后显然还有工作人员和球员。就是这样。我必须每天赢得继续保持这个水平、坐在这个椅子上并充分利用它的权利。
关于建立一个王朝：这是你必须每天去赢得的东西。我们知道现在的水平在哪里；我们知道标准在哪里；我们知道期望是什么。但好消息是，热情、激情和能量的水平甚至更高。这就是我们想要共同实现的，也是摆在我们面前的机遇。
关于凝聚俱乐部是否是他最自豪的成就：是的，以我们共同完成这一切的方式，每个人都觉得现在非常非常紧密联系在一起的一部分。然后俱乐部有非常清晰的身份、雄心和我们想要去的道路。我认为这也是非常非常重要的。
关于他是否能再干20年：就是今天，希望还有明天，这就是我们必须度过这份工作的方式。我认为你必须做的是享受这个旅程——我认为这是最重要的事情，可能也是我过去七年中最大的收获。我在这个时期得到的最大礼物就是我身边的人，他们让我感到被爱，并让我享受我所做的事情。
关于德克兰·赖斯的身体状况：我们必须管理他，因为自从他从世界杯回来后他有一些小问题，我们知道他在过去三年里踢了多少场比赛。这是明智的做法，希望明天他能上场，但其他一些球员存疑。
关于哈弗茨、孔萨和齐奥利斯的伤病：对于凯，他有肌肉拉伤，所以我跟于尔根（克洛普）谈过，他们立刻把球员送了回来，这很正常。埃兹里也带着一些问题，我们与英格兰队就此进行了良好的沟通。齐奥利斯有肌肉拉伤，他将缺席几周。他目前还无法出场。
关于辛卡皮耶和莫斯克拉的身体状况：他们都可以出场。为了能够出场对阵布莱顿的比赛，他们做得非常出色，但最终我们决定不使用他们，特别是因为我们必须在最后几分钟踢球的方式，但他们都可以出场。本·怀特也可以出场。
关于过去七年对自己最大的了解：可能你把很多精力放在你需要做的事情上，你需要帮助去做的事情，以转变足球俱乐部，达到你拥有的愿景或想法。而在那个时期内，现实也需要进行巨大的个人转变，才能达到你想去的地方。这可能是最迷人的事情之一，因为你不是一个人完成的，你是和你身边的人一起完成的，我非常非常幸运能有我身边的人。
关于他对2019年的阿尔特塔说些什么：去吧！甚至不要怀疑。但我认为这是自然的，当你对未知的事物感到恐惧时。这是你第一次做这件事，它是巨大的，它可以有如此多的责任，但你永远不知道。但如果你觉得这是正确的事情，而且你这样做的目的和理由是正确的，我认为值得冒险并去争取。

关于对阵布莱顿的失利：胃里仍然有痛感，明天我们肯定必须带着这种痛感比赛。这对我们是一个教训，从那场比赛中有很多东西要学，当你在足球比赛中没有达到某些基本要求时，特别是对阵一支非常好的球队。你变得几乎面目全非，这是可能发生的。但更多的是关于从我们是谁以及从卓越变得非常平庸的界限有多窄中吸取教训，这就是现实。但同时，也要认识到在我们拥有的困难背景下，在我们所有的国脚归队的情况下，我们在前八周所做的事情，我认为是了不起的。但是，要高度关注，因为事情变化得非常快。
关于他对利兹联本赛季开局是否感到惊讶：当我观看他们的比赛时，没有。我认为他们完全配得上他们现在的地位，因为他们赢得了它，他们之所以在那里，是因为我认为他们在比赛中做了很多伟大的事情，表现得比对手更好。我们知道他们的品质，我们在过去两天与（球员们）交谈过，我们已经为此做好了充分准备。
关于他对12点30分开球的想法：12点30分太棒了。我们已经有三周没有足球可踢了！我不知道，国脚们，我不在乎没有俱乐部足球，我们在酋长球场在我们的球迷面前踢球。因此，我们在最近几个月创造的方式和氛围是令人难以置信的，我们需要确保我们从创造这一点开始。我相信我们的球迷会非常兴奋地观看球队比赛。
关于他对球迷的信息：我的信息非常明确，我们为布莱顿发生的事情感到胃痛，这也取决于我们来消除他们仍然感受到的痛苦。这是我们的责任，我们现在需要把它带给他们。
关于他如何适应阿森纳的工作：经历不同的阶段和不同的时刻。我认为我一直是由我对这家俱乐部的激情和爱驱动的，因为我有一个梦想，那就是成为一名教练、主教练。这家俱乐部给了我立即处于最高水平的机会，我愿意做任何事情来让它发挥作用。我认为我身边有合适的人来弥补所有的不足或我不知道的事情，帮助我变得更好，并以一切可能的方式帮助球员和俱乐部每天都在进步，并灌输那种文化、那种身份和那种雄心。
关于让马克斯·道德曼保持低调：我认为这是集体责任。首先，为了父母，因为他们是花最多时间陪伴他们的人，而且他们已经赋予了让他成为今天的教育，然后是围绕他工作的每个人。但我不认为马克斯有很多迹象需要担心，因为他想做的是尽其所能在最高水平上踢好足球，他的重心就在那里。
关于他是否觉得他在曼城的时间被玷污了：我理解这个问题是从哪里来的。周围有很多噪音。这是一个正在进行中尚未解决的程序，我认为我们需要尊重它，当然我也必须尊重这一点。
关于他是否必须与球员谈论此事：这不在我们的手中。我们唯一能做的就是专注于我们能做的一切，尽我们所能做到最好，比任何其他对手都好，这就是我们投入精力的地方。
关于在本赛季解决这个问题有多重要：人们有责任管理这个程序并得出正确的结论。我确信这会完成，并且会以正确的方式解决。我们必须相信这一点。

关于在他的合同谈判期间谈论了什么：我正在谈论我们对彼此的感受。我们分析我们一起做的事情的方式，特别是我们将如何带领这家俱乐部成为世界上多年来最好的俱乐部，平台，我们拥有的好东西，然后你只是对彼此的感受有一种感觉，我们如何做事。我很幸运能让斯坦和乔治站在你面前，与他们交谈并表达他们想做什么，他们想怎么做，尤其是，这只是鼓舞人心的。然后有些事情与我有关，也有教练组有关，以及他们如何重视周围的人以及双方正在做的事情。这完全是一致的。这就是为什么当我在经历了几个月的讨论、想法以及这是不是最好的事情以及持续多长时间和其他必须讨论的事情后，看到某人感到高兴时。我只是感动，因为每个人看起来都很高兴。我非常高兴，我的家人也是，这是最重要的事情，还有工作人员、周围的人、球员和他们也是。我认为这非常重要，不仅仅是结果。

关于他为什么有足够的信心去争取统治地位：这就是我们想要尝试实现的。这就是雄心壮志，我不认为你必须隐藏它。事情是你必须每天都为之奋斗，这就是足球，但你的抱负和你的梦想就在那里。我认为实现它们更容易，如果我告诉你我刚到这里时的那些梦想，你可能会说：“你在说什么？”但那是雄心壮志，那是动力，这是因为我们相信我们可以做到。然后会有许多因素允许我们或不允许我们实现它。时间会证明一切，但这种动力肯定是存在的。
关于他是否为上赛季在球场上赢得冠军感到欣慰：当我想到我们是如何做到这一点的以及我们为了实现它必须经历的时刻时，我感到非常自豪，也非常情绪化。由于我们这样做的方式，这是一种独特而真挚的感觉。
关于他是否有任何关于签署新合同的疑虑：你有时必须停下来思考你可以这样做多久，不仅是在这里做，而且是为了你自己。你是否有适当水平的渴望、能量、你身边的人，当你说话时他们看你的方式？我的感觉是是的，如果这种感觉有一天改变了，我们会看着彼此的眼睛，就是这样。这很简单。
关于他是否认为英超联赛受到损害：那里又有一个尚未解决的程序。它正在进行中，一旦解决，我们可以有更清晰的观点。到目前为止，我还不准备发表任何评论

关于他是否认为自己在某个时候想要休息：休息？停止我正在做的事情？目前，这不在我的脑海里，因为我太喜欢我所做的事情了。我每天早晨醒来都有这种能量。很多人说：“米克尔，你有时需要休息。”但现实是，我很诚实，有时我在白天休息一下，我回去开始做一些事情，我得到了更多的能量，因为我喜欢我所做的事情。这个怎么样？如果我们通过那个怎么样？这就是不工作的魅力，做一些绝对是你的激情所在的事情，这就是为什么我感到非常幸运能在我现在的位置上。

关于他是否能在这个职位上坚持10年、15年：我不知道。我认为我仍然很年轻，这也是我的第一次经历，这可能就是我生活在职业中的方式。这周我们进行了很多讨论，人们谈论压力或紧张，我理解。我不把我的工作与此联系起来。我经历过非常不同的时刻，但更多的是关于我对比赛和所做的事情的激情和爱的水平，以及我拥有的雄心、动力和抱负，如果你想给它起个名字，可以。但对我来说，每天做这件事是一种特权。如果有一天不是，那么这也是我的决定：“好吧，现在我不喜欢它了，是时候停下来了。”
关于他是否认为这是世界上最好的联赛：100%。
关于英超联赛中严格的财务规则有多重要：我刚刚回答了这个问题，在我看来，由于很多原因，它是世界上最好的联赛，而且因为我在这里呆了20多年。它将继续成为世界上最好的联赛。再次，我感到有特权能够在我现在的位置上，事实上，还有其他俱乐部在以如此聪明和高效的方式管理他们的资源方面表现得非常出色。这是好的，因为它增加了竞争，我们在几周前看到了这一点。
关于他从布莱顿比赛中学到了什么：两件事。首先，关于比赛的第一件事，我刚才已经提到了，然后是我们的球员有多好，因为当我看着他们周游世界，为不同的国家队踢球，以及他们在国家队中产生的不可思议的影响时，这也给你带来了放心。然后，当他们来的时候，他们的脸上带着灿烂的笑容，所以他们有宾至如归的感觉，他们很高兴来到这里，这是一种极好的感觉。
关于道德曼、哈弗茨和孔萨的身体状况：马克斯可以出场，埃兹里和凯我们明天再看。
关于围绕曼城的噪音是否能帮助我们：我们所想的是关于我们自己，关于我们所做的事情，以及我们想要实现的目标。就是这样。其余的是我们无法控制的东西，我们从未控制过，我们也不想控制它。这就是我们所做事情的魅力所在，但最终很多事情取决于我们，这就是我们想要离开它的地方。
关于他是否与佩普交谈过：我们将讨论这个问题，利用正在发生的不同事情。我更愿意回答这些问题。
关于他如何看待自己七年来的演变：随着足球俱乐部或我们围绕俱乐部的球员群体的转变，显然伴随着各个层面的个人转变。做一件你一生中从未做过的事情，搬迁你的家庭，开始建立和创造一些你坚信会让很多人快乐的事情。
然后在此过程中经历一些困难时期，再次站起来，带着相同的目标拉着你周围的人，并一起度过一些不可思议的时刻。这塑造了你，这是不可避免的。这是最好的事情之一，这是这次旅程中的一份礼物。我想经历更多的转变和演变，因为这就是我们来到这里的目的，继续学习，保持好奇心并帮助人们享受这项令人难以置信的比赛。

关于如何激励球员和员工：我总是喜欢它。当面对困难时，当你必须把人带在你身边时，我认为这是我们工作中最美好的事情。把人们带上旅程，让他们觉得自己是某事的一部分，有一个非常清晰的目标，然后经历各个阶段，一章一章地，你开始接近实现所有目标，再次出发并重塑自己并做到这一点。然后是比赛的演变方式以及你如何随着比赛而演变，你能否领先于比赛。这也是一个持续的挑战，特别是考虑到联赛中经理和球队的水平，而且这不会停止。所以这也不会让你停下来。

items.titleEn: Injury latest on Havertz, Tzolis, Rice, Konsa and White
items.summaryEn: Mikel Arteta has provided an update on the fitness of his squad heading into our Premier League game against Leeds United
bodyEn: After a three-week international break, Mikel Arteta can select a starting XI again when we face Leeds United on Saturday, and he has updated us on which players he has at his disposal.

A few Gunners returned to the Sobha Realty Training Centre earlier than expected, including Kai Havertz, who was withdrawn during Germany's opening match of the four-game break against the Netherlands in Amsterdam. Christos Tzolis then picked up an injury as a substitute in Greece's draw with the Dutch, while Ezri Konsa missed England's final group match against the Czech Republic on Tuesday.

Mikel revealed he's been in close contact with all the national team managers to see how his players were faring, and while he hopes that Kai and Ezri could be OK to feature against the Whites, he'll definitely be without Christos for the next few matches.

"With Kai because he had a muscular injury," he said in his pre-match press conference. "I spoke to Jurgen [Klopp] and immediately they sent the player back, as is normal. Ezri has been carrying some issues as well, and we had good communication with the England camp about that.
"Tzolis has a muscle injury and he's going to be out I think for a few weeks. He's not available yet."

Declan Rice meanwhile sat out the entire international break, and Mikel felt that was unavoidable, with the midfielder struggling with niggles after a shorter-than-usual summer. That call should mean that Declan is raring to go against Leeds.

"We have to manage him because he's had a few issues since he's come back from the World Cup," Mikel added. "We know the amount of games he's played in the last three years. It was the sensible thing to do, and hopefully tomorrow he's available."

Thankfully, our defensive options have been bolstered by the return of Ben White, who missed out on returning to his former club, Brighton & Hove Albion, after sustaining a groin issue in the win against Sunderland last month.
He returned to training during the break, while Piero Hincapie and Cristhian Mosquera are also back to full fitness too, with Mikel praising the duo for their swift comebacks.

"They did incredibly well to be available for the Brighton game," he said. "We decided not to use them at the end, especially in the manner that we had to play the last few minutes, but they are both available, and Ben White as well."

Max Dowman was forced to pull out of England’s under-19s squad last weekend after appearing in all three matches this international break against the Republic of Ireland, Norway and the United States, but Mikel also said that the 16-year-old is available if need be.

items.titleZh: 哈弗茨、佐利斯、赖斯、孔萨和怀特的最新伤情
items.summaryZh: 米克尔·阿尔特塔介绍了球队在对阵利兹联前的伤病情况。
bodyZh: 经过三周的国际比赛日后，米克尔·阿尔特塔在周六对阵利兹联时可以重新选择首发阵容，他向我们更新了目前可用的球员情况。
几名阿森纳球员比预期更早返回索布哈疗养地训练中心，其中包括哈弗茨，他在德国队对阵荷兰队的四场比赛的首场比赛中被换下。此后，佐利斯在希腊战平荷兰的比赛中替补登场时受伤，而孔萨则缺席了英格兰周二对阵捷克共和国的最后一场小组赛。
米克尔透露，他一直与所有国家队主教练保持密切联系，以了解球员的表现，虽然他希望凯和埃兹里能够出战利兹联，但他肯定会在接下来几场比赛中缺少克里斯托斯。
他在赛前新闻发布会上表示：“关于凯，因为他有肌肉损伤。我跟于尔根沟通过，他们立刻把球员送了回来，这是正常的。埃兹里也一直带着一些小伤，我们与英格兰队就此保持了良好的沟通。”
“佐利斯有肌肉损伤，我认为他将缺席几周。他现在还无法出场。”
与此同时，赖斯缺席了整个国际比赛日，米克尔认为这是不可避免的，这位中场球员在经历了一个比平时短的夏天后一直在与小伤作斗争。这一决定意味着赖斯已经蓄势待发，准备迎战利兹联。
米克尔补充道：“我们必须管理好他，因为自从他世界杯归来后就遇到了一些问题。我们知道他在过去三年里踢了多少场比赛。这是明智的做法，希望明天他能出场。”
值得庆幸的是，本·怀特的回归增强了我们的防守选择，他在上个月对阵桑德兰的比赛中腹股沟受伤，错失了重返老东家布赖顿的机会。
他在国际比赛日期间恢复了训练，同时皮罗·因卡皮耶和克里斯蒂安·莫斯克拉也完全恢复了健康，米克尔称赞这两人复苏迅速。
他说道：“他们表现得非常出色，能够赶上对阵布赖顿的比赛。我们决定最终不使用他们，特别是考虑到我们在最后几分钟必须采取的踢法，但他们都可以出场，本·怀特也是。”
马克斯·道德曼上周末在参加了对阵爱尔兰、挪威和美国的全部三场国际比赛后，被迫退出了英格兰U19代表队，但米克尔也表示，如果有需要，这位16岁的球员可以出场。

items.titleEn: U21s preview: Arsenal v Sunderland
items.summaryEn: Our young Gunners chase the Black Cats for a first PL2 win of the season
bodyEn: Our young Gunners are still hunting for their first Premier League 2 win of the campaign, with Sunderland next up on Saturday, October 10.
The match will take place at the Mangata Developments Stadium, with kick-off scheduled for 1pm (UK time).
David Horseman's side have picked up three draws and a loss from their opening fixture quartet, with the recent goalless draw at Birmingham City leaving us with work to do to kick-start the season.
THE OPPOSITION
The Black Cats have enjoyed a strong start to 2026/27, finding three wins from four and scoring plenty along the way to sit fifth in the league standings.
The North East outfit netted 12 times to beat Nottingham Forest, Ipswich Town and Norwich City, but took a hit to their goal difference during a 5-1 loss to Brentford in late August.
In Premier League International Cup action, the Mackems began Group D with a point against Dutch side PSV Eindhoven, drawing 1-1 at the Stadium of Light.
We last faced Sunderland in March, losing 3-1 at Eppleton Colliery Football Ground where Andre Harriman-Annous' second-half finish proved only a consolation.
HOW TO WATCH
As with all Premier League 2 fixtures, entry to Saturday's game at Mangata Developments Stadium is free, so get down to the ground to cheer on our under-21s.

Live updates will also be available on our Academy's X account, with a full match report, highlights and interviews with head coach David Horseman and one of our young Gunners to follow after the game.

items.summaryZh: 年轻的枪手们将迎战黑猫，力争赛季首场英超2联赛胜利。
bodyZh: 我们的年轻枪手仍在寻找本赛季英超2联赛的首场胜利，10月10日星期六，他们将迎来下一个对手桑德兰。
比赛将在芒加塔发展体育场进行，开球时间定于英国时间下午1点。
戴维·霍斯曼的球队在前四场比赛中取得了三场平局和一场失利，最近客场对阵伯明翰城的互交白卷意味着我们需要努力开启本赛季的胜利步伐。
对手情况
黑猫在2026/27赛季迎来了强劲开局，在四场比赛中赢了三场并打入大量进球，目前在联赛积分榜上排名第五。

items.titleEn: Arsenal in the Community: Supporting mental health
items.summaryEn: How Arsenal in the Community support mental health
bodyEn: As we look ahead to World Mental Health Day, Arsenal in the Community is proud to highlight a range of programmes that support and promote positive mental wellbeing across our local community.

While the programmes below have a specific focus on mental health, we recognise that all of our programmes at Arsenal in the Community have a positive impact on people’s wellbeing. Whether it’s meeting new people, having a safe space to be active, building confidence or simply feeling a sense of belonging, sport can play an important role in helping people feel connected and supported.
Through strong partnerships and the power of sport, our programmes provide safe spaces, meaningful support and opportunities for people of all ages to connect, grow and thrive.
Together Against Suicide

This season, Arsenal Football Club and the North London NHS Foundation Trust are teaming up for the second season for a matchday mental health drop-in service at The Arsenal Hub, with a particular focus on suicide prevention.

The Premier League funded 11 clubs to deliver the Together Against Suicide initiative during the 2025/26 season, raising awareness of suicide prevention and providing accessible support for fans who may need it most. Following the success of the initiative, the programme has been renewed for the 2026/27 season and expanded to 20 Premier League clubs, allowing even more communities and supporters to access vital support and resources.

A North London NHS Foundation Trust practitioner will be based at The Arsenal Hub during every Arsenal Premier League home match throughout the season. Supporters will be able to access confidential conversations and guidance without an appointment, simply by walking into the Hub, where they will be welcomed by staff.
The practitioner will also be able to provide information about local mental health and support services where appropriate.
The service will be available ahead of the Leeds fixture on Saturday 10th October.
Located next to Emirates Stadium at 56 Benwell Road, N7 7BA, The Arsenal Hub will be open from two hours before kick-off, throughout the match, and for one hour after full-time.
For more information about the programme, please email togetheragainstsuicide@arsenal.co.uk.
Brandon Centre Connect and Girls Kicks

Arsenal in the Community’s partnership with Brandon Centre is rooted in the Brandon Connect service, which provides therapeutic outreach sessions at The Arsenal Hub for young people who may otherwise struggle to access or engage with mental health services.

Together, the organisations also deliver Arsenal Girls’ Kicks, football sessions supported by a sports psychologist that help girls develop emotional awareness, communication skills and resilience as they continue to grow as young people.

This partnership demonstrates the positive impact that sport and community organisations can have when working together to support mental wellbeing and create meaningful change within local communities.
For more information about the Brandon Centre, please contact GeoffreyBaruch@brandoncentre.org.uk.
Advantage Mentoring - Talking Tactics Programme
Since 2020, Arsenal in the Community has partnered with Advantage Mentoring to deliver Talking Tactics, an innovative mental health mentoring programme supporting young people across north London.

Talking Tactics is a one-to-one mentoring programme for young people aged 11 to 21 who are experiencing mild to moderate mental health challenges. Delivered in a familiar and engaging environment at local football clubs, the programme combines mentoring support with the positive influence of sport.
Participants receive weekly one-to-one mentoring sessions for up to six months, working with a qualified mentor to set goals, build resilience and develop strategies to cope with life’s challenges.
To find out more about Talking Tactics, please contact Advantage Mentoring Coordinator Gemma Benham at gbenham@arsenal.co.uk.
NLFT Mental Health Programme
Arsenal in the Community works in partnership with the North London NHS Foundation Trust (NLFT) to deliver weekly football sessions for adults living with mental health conditions.

Sessions take place at The Arsenal Hub, where Arsenal coaches work alongside a qualified mental health practitioner to create a safe, supportive and inclusive environment for participants experiencing mental health challenges.
While our coaches lead the football activity, the NLFT practitioner is on hand to provide additional support throughout the sessions, helping participants feel comfortable and engaged.
Running since 2010, the programme has become an important part of many participants’ weekly routines, with some members attending for more than a decade.

As well as promoting physical activity, the sessions help improve mental wellbeing, reduce social isolation and create opportunities for participants to build positive friendships and support networks.
For more information, please contact Accessibility Coordinator Luke Howard at lhoward@arsenal.co.uk.

items.titleZh: 阿森纳社区：支持心理健康
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳社区项目致力于通过体育和合作伙伴关系支持心理健康。
bodyZh: 值此世界心理健康日来临之际，阿森纳社区很荣幸地重点介绍一系列旨在支持和促进当地社区积极心理健康的计划。
尽管以下计划特别关注心理健康，但我们认识到阿森纳社区的所有计划都对人们的福祉产生了积极影响。无论是结识新朋友、拥有一个充满活力且安全的空间、建立自信还是仅仅感受到归属感，体育都能在帮助人们建立联系和获得支持方面发挥重要作用。
通过紧密的合作和体育的力量，我们的计划为所有年龄段的人们提供安全的空间、有意义的支持以及建立联系、成长和蓬勃发展的机会。
携手反对自杀
本赛季，阿森纳足球俱乐部与北伦敦NHS基金信托基金会连续第二个赛季在阿森纳中心合作推出比赛日心理健康临时咨询服务，重点关注自杀预防。
在英超联赛的资助下，11家俱乐部在2025/26赛季开展了“携手反对自杀”倡议，提高人们对自杀预防的认识，并为最需要的球迷提供便捷的支持。随着该倡议的成功，该项目已续签至2026/27赛季，并扩展至20家英超俱乐部，使更多的社区和支持者能够获得至关重要的支持与资源。
在整个赛季阿森纳的每一场英超主场比赛期间，北伦敦NHS基金信托基金会的一名执业医师将常驻阿森纳中心。支持者只需走进中心，在工作人员的迎接下，即可无需预约获得保密的对话和指导。
在适当情况下，执业医师还将能够提供有关当地心理健康和支持服务的信息。
该服务将在10月10日星期六对阵利兹联的比赛前提供。
阿森纳中心位于酋长球场旁边的本韦尔路56号（邮编：N7 7BA），开放时间为开赛前两小时、整场比赛期间以及终场哨响后一小时。
有关该项目的更多信息，请发送电子邮件至togetheragainstsuicide@arsenal.co.uk。
布兰登中心连接与女子计划
阿森纳社区与布兰登中心的合作植根于布兰登连接服务，该服务在阿森纳中心为那些可能难以接触或参与心理健康服务的年轻人提供治疗性外展课程。
这两个组织还共同举办了阿森纳女子足球计划，这是一项由体育心理学家支持的足球课程，旨在帮助女孩在成长过程中培养情感意识、沟通技巧和韧性。
这一合作展示了体育和社区组织在共同努力支持心理健康并在当地社区创造有意义的改变时所产生的积极影响。
有关布兰登中心的更多信息，请联系GeoffreyBaruch@brandoncentre.org.uk。
优势指导 - 战术谈话计划
自2020年以来，阿森纳社区与优势指导合作开展了“战术谈话”项目，这是一项创新的心理健康指导计划，旨在支持北伦敦各地的年轻人。
“战术谈话”是一项针对11至21岁面临轻度至中度心理健康挑战的年轻人的对一指导计划。该计划在当地足球俱乐部熟悉且引人入胜的环境中进行，将指导支持与体育的积极影响结合起来。
参与者每周接受长达六个月的一对一指导课程，与合格的导师合作设定目标、建立韧性并制定应对生活挑战的策略。
要了解有关“战术谈话”的更多信息，请联系优势指导协调员Gemma Benham：gbenham@arsenal.co.uk。
北伦敦NHS基金信托基金会心理健康项目
阿森纳社区与北伦敦NHS基金信托基金会合作，为患有心理健康疾病的成年人提供每周一次的足球课程。
课程在阿森纳中心举行，阿森纳教练与合格的心理健康执业医师合作，为面临心理健康挑战的参与者创建一个安全、支持和包容的环境。
虽然我们的教练负责主导足球活动，但北伦敦NHS基金信托基金会的执业医师随时准备在整个课程中提供额外的支持，帮助参与者感到舒适和投入。
该项目自2010年开始运行，已成为许多参与者每周生活的重要组成部分，一些成员已经参加了十多年。
除了促进体育锻炼外，这些课程还有助于改善心理健康、减少社会孤立，并为参与者建立积极的友谊和支持网络创造机会。
欲了解更多信息，请联系无障碍协调员Luke Howard：lhoward@arsenal.co.uk。

bodyEn: Declan Rice’s future role in England’s midfield was questioned by Gary Lineker after Alex Scott’s impressive first senior international start in the 7-0 thrashing of Croatia. But the decision to withdraw from Thomas Tuchel’s squad in an attempt to manage his workload made sense after Rice had only three weeks off post-World Cup before returning to pre-season training. The 27-year-old has struggled with persistent back problems after suffering a hamstring injury last December and Mikel Arteta will hope that the rest has done Rice – who is thought to be close to agreeing a lucrative new contract at the Emirates – the world of good as they prepare to resume the defence of their Premier League title against Leeds on Saturday. Ed Aarons
Arsenal v Leeds, Saturday 12.30pm (all times BST)

Several Aston Villa players shone for their countries during the international window but one of those who stayed with the club may have made the biggest impression on Unai Emery. Villa’s remaining squad went to Spain for a mid-season training camp, including Alejandro Garnacho, whose last cap for Argentina was almost two years ago. Garnacho has been lesser-spotted in a Villa shirt, playing just 31 minutes as a substitute, but scored in both of Villa’s friendlies during the break, against Southampton and Sevilla. The 22-year-old, who joined Villa on loan from Chelsea in the summer with a conditional obligation, was an unused substitute for their past four matches but is he now primed to affect games? Villa are hopeful Emery has unlocked Garnacho, who has struggled for form since leaving Manchester United. “Ready now!” Garnacho posted on social media last weekend and Villa will hope that is the case. Ben Fisher
Aston Villa v Brentford, Saturday 3pm

With Eli Junior Kroupi, Amine Adli, Veljko Milosavljevic and Julián Araujo yet to feature this season due to injury, Marco Rose must have been tearing his remaining hair out upon learning Alex Scott got hurt on England duty and will be out of action for two months. Sitting 17th and still searching for their first league win, the German’s side squandered nine points from winning positions in four of their first five games – and it was the 23-year-old who was central in ensuring Bournemouth had those leads in the first place. With just 55 minutes of football behind him this season, it seems unlikely Alex Toth will get the nod to replace Scott when Bournemouth travel to Chelsea with the older, more experienced Ryan Christie available and in good form. But having forced his way into the Hungary starting lineup during the international break it would be no surprise to see the 20-year-old get more minutes with a view to being used far more often given his side’s gruelling schedule of nine matches in the next month. Barry Glendenning
Chelsea v Bournemouth, Saturday 3pm

Ipswich’s place in mid-table, their total of six points, came via victories over Sunderland and Crystal Palace. Gary O’Neil’s team were presented with a tough opening schedule, and while defeated by Manchester United, Liverpool and Arsenal, their manager has not allowed those reverses to dilute team spirit. Speaking to the media following the home defeat by Liverpool, O’Neil painted an ultra-positive picture that defied most observers’ view of a game beyond his team’s reach from the early stages. Thus far, a successful strategy, certainly by comparison to early season at winless Fulham. Like O’Neil, Álvaro Arbeloa is new to his job. An improved performance in the draw against United did not result in a victory Fulham deserved, though there were signs of the progressive, attacking football the arrival of the former Real Madrid interim promised. Much of the burden has fallen on Josh King, the teenager building on last year’s breakthrough season. John Brewin
Ipswich v Fulham, Saturday 3pm

Still in the Carabao Cup, with a Europa League campaign to negotiate and just four points acquired from their opening five Premier League excursions, the games are about to start coming thick and fast for a Sunderland side whose ability to cope with such a hectic schedule remains to be seen. Having lost Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey to hamstring injuries during the international break, Régis Le Bris will have to reshuffle his pack against a free-scoring Brighton side who make the 700-mile round trip to Wearside for their first game since embarrassing Arsenal three weeks ago. While Wilson Isidor will almost certainly deputise for Brobbey, Ballard’s centre-back berth will be filled by either Omar Alderete or Nordi Mukiele. Having shipped five last time out against Manchester City, a Sunderland defence that had looked conspicuously porous in the early stages of this season will need all their focus if they are to stop the gallop of a team that have already scored 16 goals. BG.
Sunderland v Brighton, Saturday 3pm

If “Dr Tottenham” is a thing, Manchester United possess their own healing powers for opponents. Self-harm is a factor too. They rolled out the welcome mat to Premier League newcomers Hull on opening day and Brighton were ushered back into a Carabao Cup tie. In United’s final game before the international break flagging Fulham were able to restore some faith, their goal via slapstick defending from Lisandro Martínez and Senne Lammens. Can Old Trafford, where fans will have regulatory matters at City to celebrate, lift the gloom for Tottenham? This season, like last season and the one before that, Spurs have assumed the mantle of crisis club, a status Michael Carrick’s January arrival temporarily removed from United. Lose to Tottenham, and the crisis prefix is likely to be reattached. Tottenham have done damage before. In September 2024, a 3-0 Spurs win at Old Trafford began Erik ten Hag’s hurtle towards the exit. Losing the Europa League final started Ruben Amorim’s downward spiral. Carrick beware? JB
Manchester United v Tottenham, Saturday 5.30pm

All eyes will be on Oliver Glasner as he returns to Selhurst Park with Nottingham Forest on an afternoon that will be emotionally charged for both sets of supporters and in the boardroom. The Crystal Palace chair, Steve Parish, sought to defuse tensions last week when he urged fans to “buck the trend” by welcoming the manager who led the south London club to the first three major trophies in their history in the space of 12 months. “I would be mortified if he gets anything other than the roof blown off,” said Parish. But given the strength of feeling towards Forest and their owner, Evangelos Marinakis – who is still blamed by some for Palace’s demotion to the Conference League at the expense of Forest last season – many have still not forgiven Glasner for joining their rivals and could still make their feelings known when the Austrian takes his seat in the dugout before kick-off. EA
Crystal Palace v Nottingham Forest, Sunday 2pm

In Sergej Jakirovic and David Moyes, Hull City and Everton boast two of the more “pragmatic” managers in the Premier League. Renowned for their safety-first defensive styles, both teams are happy to surrender possession, rank among the top flight’s lowest sides in pass completion rates, and rely on rapid transitions and set pieces for a major share of their total expected goals. A game featuring two defences that pride themselves on their obduracy may well be settled by a well-delivered dead ball into a packed penalty area. While it may not be aesthetically pleasing, expect to see the massed ranks of defenders on both sides spending much of Sunday afternoon bracing themselves for rearguard action while peering towards the sky. The last time these sides met in the Premier League, Everton ran out easy 4-0 winners. A decade on, the aerial traffic is unlikely to be quite so one-way. BG
Hull City v Everton, Sunday 2pm

Manchester City resume playing under the darkest of clouds, with a visit to their greatest rivals of a golden period now shrouded by a guilty verdict. Five Premier League wins from five under Enzo Maresca had offered hopes of success in a post-Pep Guardiola era. The dial has since moved on what constitutes success for a club where minds are consumed by legal issues but the band must play on. Can Maresca summon a siege mentality? City lifted a treble, including the Champions League, when the 100-plus charges first came to public light in 2023. The Anfield crowd will readily remind City of the infamy their club faces down. That Guardiola’s now-disputed dominance came at the cost of Jürgen Klopp’s great team will add to the ire, and very probably the pyro greeting to Anfield. Cool heads may be required in the policing and on the field, to which a return to focusing on football may offer welcome relief. JB
Liverpool v Manchester City, Sunday 4.30pm

International football’s incursions have curbed the adrenaline rush of Coventry’s win at Nottingham Forest and Jay Dasilva’s brilliant goal, his club’s first in the top division since 2001. That gave Frank Lampard foundations to build on, a blueprint, where Forest were allowed to blow themselves out before Dasilva’s strike came on the counter. It was Stephen Mfuni, 18, on loan from Manchester City, who starred in that rearguard effort on his Premier League debut. Coventry now seek a first Premier League goal at a stadium opened in 2005, after the club’s long decline had set in. Newcastle this week passed five years of the ownership of a consortium led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. There have been two seasons of Champions League football, a trophy lifted and yet a sense of unfulfilled promise. Matthias Jaissle is leading the second phase of a jagged development process, this season’s positive signs tempered by reverses such as the 4-1 defeat by Leeds, shows how far Coventry must travel. JB
Coventry v Newcastle, Monday 8pm
